skill.name: documentation
skill.description: Create API, technical, architecture, migration, and changelog documentation with templates, examples, and publishing guidance.
skill.summary: Documentation assistant for API references, guides, ADRs, migration plans, and changelogs.
skill.author: Joseph OBrien

security_audit.summary: The static findings are documentation examples, placeholder credentials, Markdown code fences, and writing guidance. I found no evidence of executable malware behavior, live network exfiltration, real secret access, or prompt injection in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Placeholder API keys trigger secret-detection patterns.
remediation.suggestion: Use clearly non-secret placeholders such as <replace-with-your-api-key> and state that examples are not live credentials.

remediation.issue: Example commands and URLs trigger execution and network heuristics.
remediation.suggestion: Label command snippets as examples and keep placeholder domains or variables clearly non-production.

content.value_statement: Technical teams need clear docs across APIs, releases, and migrations. This skill creates structured documentation with templates and practical examples.
actual_capabilities: Creates OpenAPI and Swagger-style API documentation structures.
Writes developer guides, user guides, tutorials, and README content.
Generates changelog and release-note drafts from commit context.
Creates migration guides with upgrade steps, rollback notes, and verification checklists.
Documents architecture decisions, design specifications, and technical rationale.
Provides reusable templates for common engineering documentation formats.
limitations: Requires accurate project context, API details, or commit history from the user.
Generated examples should be reviewed and tested before publication.
Does not validate live APIs unless the host agent is given separate tools and permission.
Placeholder URLs, tokens, and package names must be replaced before use.

use_cases.title: Document a new API release
use_cases.description: Create endpoint references, authentication notes, examples, and versioning guidance for a public or internal API.

use_cases.title: Prepare customer release notes
use_cases.description: Turn technical commits into clear changelog entries grouped by features, fixes, improvements, and breaking changes.

use_cases.title: Plan an upgrade path
use_cases.description: Create migration documentation with prerequisites, breaking changes, upgrade steps, rollback guidance, and validation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Create a README
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner documentation task for a project landing page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a README for this project. Include the purpose, installation steps, quick start, main features, configuration, troubleshooting, and license notes.

prompt_templates.title: Document API endpoints
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate task for endpoint reference documentation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create API documentation for these endpoints. Include authentication, request parameters, response fields, error cases, examples, and versioning notes.

prompt_templates.title: Write a migration guide
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced task for version upgrades and breaking changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a migration guide from version A to version B. Include prerequisites, breaking changes, step-by-step upgrade instructions, rollback steps, and verification checks.

prompt_templates.title: Generate release documentation
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced task using commit history and a release style guide.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate customer-facing release notes from these commits. Group changes by impact, rewrite technical language, call out breaking changes, and follow this style guide.

output_examples.input: Create API docs for user and workspace endpoints.
output_examples.output: A structured API reference with endpoint summaries, authentication requirements, parameters, response descriptions, errors, and usage examples.

output_examples.input: Generate a changelog from the last release commits.
output_examples.output: Customer-facing release notes grouped into new features, improvements, fixes, security updates, and breaking changes.

output_examples.input: Write a migration guide for a major version upgrade.
output_examples.output: An upgrade guide with prerequisites, changed behavior, ordered migration steps, rollback instructions, and a verification checklist.

best_practices: Provide real project context, target audience, and publishing format before requesting documentation.
Review generated examples against the current codebase before sharing them externally.
Keep generated documentation close to source changes so updates stay accurate.
anti_patterns: Do not publish placeholder credentials, URLs, package names, or commands without review.
Do not ask for broad documentation without source material or audience details.
Do not treat generated release notes as final without product and engineering review.

faq.question: Can this skill create OpenAPI documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. It can draft OpenAPI-style structures, endpoint descriptions, schemas, authentication notes, and examples from provided API details.

faq.question: Can it generate changelogs from commits?
faq.answer: Yes. It can organize commit context into customer-facing release notes and changelog sections.

faq.question: Does it execute SDK generators?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and documentation patterns, but execution depends on the host agent and user permission.

faq.question: Is it useful for non-API documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. It also supports README files, user guides, tutorials, design specs, ADRs, and migration guides.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the audience, source material, product behavior, API details, version changes, and any style requirements.

faq.question: Should generated docs be reviewed?
faq.answer: Yes. Review examples, commands, links, and release notes before publishing them to users.
